title: Scaena deck document
description: Canonical deck.json. A deck is a scene graph (nodes) plus an ordered cue list (states) over a narrative spine, rendered against a theme. See docs/SPEC.md §3.

formats.description: Additional projections rendered from the same spine and nodes with other layout template sets.

theme.description: Path to a theme file inside the bundle, or an inline theme object (schema: theme.schema.json).

furniture.description: What each slide shows of the theme's furniture (deck format 0.19, ADR-0028): its number, and the words at its foot.

nodes.description: The scene graph. Keys are node ids, stable across the whole deck.

states.description: The cue list, in order. Every click is a state.

overrides.description: Per node, props that win over its theme, its defaults, and every state: a delta merged into the node as each state resolves it (SPEC §3.6). The only place raw pixel and color values are theme-legal (lint W300 elsewhere).

drift.description: In shorter sides of the rect.

angle.description: Degrees clockwise from up: a linear gradient's direction (180, the default, runs top to bottom), a conic one's start.

x.description: A radial or conic gradient's center across the rect, 0 to 1 within it, and as far as its width again either side outside it (deck format 0.34).

y.description: A radial or conic gradient's center down the rect, likewise.

radius.description: A radial gradient's radius, in shorter sides of the rect.

speed.description: Degrees a second a linear or conic gradient turns.

octaves.description: Layers of finer noise over the first (fractal Brownian motion); 1 is plain simplex noise.

speed.description: How fast the field changes, in noise cycles a second.

contrast.description: How far the field spreads across the palette.

fps.description: How many times a second the grain changes; 0 holds it still.

size.description: A particle's radius, in shorter sides of the rect.

softness.description: How much of a particle's radius its edge fades over.

scale.description: A cell of the light's network, in shorter sides of the rect.

speed.description: How fast the light wobbles and flows.

intensity.description: How far along the palette a line's middle reaches.

Format.description: Additional projections rendered from the same spine and nodes with other layout template sets.

ThemeRef.description: A theme file inside the bundle, or an inline theme object (schema: theme.schema.json).

Furniture.description: What a deck shows on each slide of its theme's furniture (deck format 0.19, ADR-0028).

number.description: Each slide's number, counted from 1 in the deck's order, where the theme places it.

footer.description: Words at each slide's foot, where the theme places them: a company, a date, `Confidential`.

fetched.description: Where its rows came from (ADR-0030, deck format 0.31): a forecast fetched once into the deck, credited at the foot of each chart or table that reads it.

SourceRef.description: A data file in the bundle, or rows inline.

Fetched.description: Where an object came from (ADR-0030, decision 2).

from.description: The service, by Scaena's name for it: one of `SERVICES`.

at.description: When its answer came, an instant in UTC (RFC 3339), by the clock of the client that asked.

asked.description: What the person asked for, as typed: an address, a place, or `lat, lon`.

credit.description: What the service's terms ask shown with it, as runs, each linked where it says.

license.description: The data's license, where the service names one: `ODbL-1.0`.

map.description: A map's view, as it was asked (PLAN O.1b).

terms.description: Which of the service's terms applied, where the request itself says so: Open-Meteo's `free` service or its `customer` one (deck format 0.31).

kept.description: The person keeps it as of its date: lint does not judge its date (W428).

edited.description: Its rows were edited since they came, which the credit says, as CC BY asks.

forecast.description: A forecast, as it was asked (PLAN O.2a): the place, the period, and the units.

stock.description: A price series, as it was asked and as far as it runs (PLAN O.3a, deck format 0.33).

CreditRun.description: A run of a credit: its words, and where they link.

link.description: A web address the words link to.

MapAsked.description: A map's picture as it was asked (ADR-0030, decisions 11–12): the place, the view, and the size.

place.description: The place the pin marks, as the geocoder named it, or the coordinates typed.

zoom.description: The service's zoom, 1 to 20: each step doubles the scale.

style.description: The service's style, by its name: `positron`, `dark-matter`, or `osm-bright`.

size.description: The picture's size as asked, in the service's points: the box in canvas units.

scale.description: Pixels to a point: 2 asks for a picture twice as dense.

name.description: Its name, as the geocoder gave it.

LatLon.description: A point on the earth, in degrees.

Terms.description: Which of a service's terms a fetch came under.

oneOf.description: The service's free terms: Open-Meteo's, for non-commercial use.
The terms of the user's own subscription: Open-Meteo's `customer-` hosts.

Forecast.description: What a forecast was fetched for (ADR-0030, decision 18): the place, the period, and the units.

period.description: Whether each row is a day or an hour.

units.description: The units its figures came in.

Place2.description: The place a forecast is for, as the geocoder named it.

region.description: The region it is in, where the geocoder names one: `Massachusetts`.

zone.description: Its time zone, by its IANA name: `America/New_York`.

offset.description: The offset from UTC, in seconds, its days were cut by when it was fetched: `-14400`.

Period.description: A forecast's period: each row a day or an hour.

Units.description: The units a forecast's figures are in: metric (°C, km/h, mm) or US (°F, mph, inches).

Stock.description: A price series as it was fetched (ADR-0030, decision 22): the symbol, the range, where it trades and in what, and the last price's civil time there. Its rows are `time`, `close`, and `base`, in a CSV under `data/`.

symbol.description: The ticker symbol, as the service names it: `AAPL`.

range.description: How far back the series runs.

exchange.description: The exchange it trades on, as the service names it: `NASDAQ`.

currency.description: The currency its prices are in, ISO 4217: `USD`.

zone.description: The exchange's time zone, by its IANA name, in which the rows' times are civil: `America/New_York`.

through.description: The last price's civil time in the exchange's zone: a day, `2026-10-15`, or a close at its bar's end, `2026-10-15T16:00`.

Range.description: How far back a price series runs: a day, a week, a month, three months, a year, or the year to date.

Id.description: A slug: unique within its collection (SPEC §3.2).

claim.description: One sentence the audience should leave with.

notes.description: Speaker notes: what a presenter reads for each state it names that has none of its own (SPEC §2.6).

duration.description: Estimated seconds: what a video and the spine give its states with no `hold`, less their cues (SPEC §2.4).

Node.description: A node in the scene graph: its `type` and that type's properties. A node's type never changes across states (E104).

NodeProps.description: The properties every node type has (SPEC §3.3); each type adds its own.

alt.description: Accessible description; text nodes default to their content (SPEC §3.12).

locked.description: Locked in an editor (PLAN 2.95): its canvas passes over the node, and moves, resizes, turns, retypes, and deletes nothing of it; its layers and its inspector select it and unlock it. The node's own, in every state: a state and `overrides` cannot set it (E104). It draws as it would unlocked.

shadow.description: The shadow it casts (PLAN 2.115): one of the theme's by name, or one written out.

formats.description: How it lays out in another of the deck's formats, by format (SPEC §3.4, ADR-0020): each property there takes the place of the node's own of the same name when the deck lays out in that format.

TextNode.description: Typographic text (SPEC §3.5): `text` or `runs`, set in a theme role.

style.description: What this node changes about its role's look (SPEC §3.6).

maxSize.description: The most its size may grow to under `fit: grow`; under `fit: shrink`, where it is under the text's size, the most it is set at (deck format 0.36).

measure.description: Max line length in characters (overrides the role's).

list.description: Its paragraphs as a list's items (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0018): one entry for each paragraph a hard line break ends, in order, `null` for one that is no item. Paragraphs past its end are no items.

paragraphs.description: The paragraphs a state draws (PLAN 2.129, deck format 0.27), counted from 1: one, or the first and the last of a run. The rest are laid out where they stand and not drawn, so a list built by bullet keeps its place as its items come and go. Without it, all.

code.description: The text is code (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0029; deck format 0.28): set as written, its lines broken only where it breaks them, its tabs standing to stops, grown then shrunk to fit its box, never under 12 pt.

ShapeNode.description: Vector geometry: `path` (SVG path data) or a `kind`.

view.description: The box of the path's own coordinates that fits the node's box, [x, y, w, h], as SVG's `viewBox`: the path is scaled alike both ways to fit it and centered in the node's box, so icons drawn on one view keep one weight beside each other (PLAN 2.104). Without one, the path's own bounds fit.

connect.description: The two nodes a line or an arrow joins (PLAN 2.109): it runs from `from`'s box to `to`'s as each state lays them out, and so follows them, and it leaves wherever either does. What it joins places it: it takes no `at` and no `points` of its own.

ends.description: What a line's or an arrow's ends are drawn with (PLAN 2.128, deck format 0.27): its `start`, where its first point is, and its `end`. An end it does not name is a line's bare end, and an arrow's last a filled head.

ImageNode.description: An image from the bundle, a PNG or a JPEG, placed in its box (SPEC §3.3).

src.description: The image file's path in the bundle; `assets/<sha256>.<ext>` once saved.

focal.description: The point of the image that lines up with the same point of the box, in fractions of the crop, as CSS `object-position`; default [0.5, 0.5].

crop.description: The part of the image to show, [x, y, w, h] in fractions of the image.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of what shows.

mask.description: Shows the image only inside a shape (PLAN 2.113), fitted to what shows, as a presentation app masks a picture with a shape: an oval, or a polygon of the shape library. It takes the place of `radius`.

adjust.description: Its light and color adjusted (PLAN 2.117), as a presentation app's Adjust Image adjusts a picture.

fetched.description: Where the picture came from (ADR-0030, deck format 0.29): a map fetched once from a service, with when, what was asked, and the credit its terms ask shown with it, which the engine draws.

pin.description: A pin the engine draws on the picture (ADR-0030, decision 13), with its label.

credit.description: Where its `fetched` credit is drawn: on a card inside the picture (the default), or as a line below it inside the box.

ChartNode.description: A data-bound chart (SPEC §3.7): a declarative spec compiled to marks.

orient.description: Which way a `bar`'s or a `stackedBar`'s bars run (PLAN 1.29): up from the baseline, the default, or across it, the categories down the side and their names read across. Any other kind is E106.

dataTransform.description: Steps run in order before the chart reads its data: filter, derive, sort, limit, aggregate, fold, pivot (SPEC §3.10; expressions in docs/spec/expr.md).

interval.description: A `range`'s interval about each value (PLAN 1.30): the fields that hold its low and high ends. Any other kind is E106.

facet.description: Small multiples (PLAN 1.31): a panel for each value of a field, on one shared scale, each named by its value.

projected.description: Which of a line's or an area's rows are a forecast or an estimate (PLAN 1.28).

key.description: The field that identifies a mark across states.

weather.description: A `weather` chart's fields, units, and parts (deck format 0.32, ADR-0030): any other kind is E106.

TableNode.description: A data-bound table (SPEC §3.3): rows from a data source, set in the theme's `tables` styles, each row matched by `key` across states.

dataTransform.description: Steps run in order before the table reads its data (SPEC §3.10).

columns.description: Its columns, in order; every column of the data when unset.

key.description: The field that identifies a row across states; the first column's when unset.

header.description: The header row, shown unless false.

ShaderNode.description: A parametric background or fill (SPEC §3.8): a kind, a seed, a theme palette, and typed params, its own or a theme preset's. No shader source, ever.

palette.description: A shader palette from the theme; the preset's when unset.

preset.description: A shader preset from the theme, of this kind: its palette and params are this node's, unless the node sets its own.

StackNode.description: A layout container along one axis (CSS flex, SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent`.

axis.description: `y` (the default) stacks children top to bottom, `x` left to right.

distribute.description: Where leftover space along the axis goes: `start` (the default), `center`, `end`, or between and around the children.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of the container's `fill` and `stroke`.

GridNode.description: A layout container on a grid of its own (CSS grid, SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent` and take an `area`, a `col`/`row` range, or the next free cell.

areas.description: Named areas, one string per row of cells, as CSS `grid-template-areas`: `["head head", "left right"]`; `.` leaves a cell unnamed.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of the container's `fill` and `stroke`.

FrameNode.description: A layout container whose children place themselves by `at.rect`, relative to its padding (SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent`.

radius.description: Rounds the corners of the container's `fill` and `stroke`.

GroupNode.description: Nodes drawn together, each placed on the slide by its own `at` (SPEC §3.4). Its children name it in `at.parent`.

Semantic.description: Communicative function, independent of visual role (SPEC §3.3). Reserved for narrative lints; optional.

Color.description: Theme token name (e.g. "accent", "color.ink") or a literal (#rrggbb[aa], oklch(...)). Literals outside overrides are lint W300.

Length.description: A length in canvas units, a token reference (e.g. "space.4"), or a percentage string.

ShadowRef.description: The shadow a node casts (PLAN 2.115): the theme's shadow of this name (`tokens.shadow`), or one written out, an override: `x`, `y`, and `blur` in canvas units, a `color`, and an `opacity`. A filled rectangle or ellipse, an image, and a container's panel cast one.

WrittenShadow.description: A shadow written out (PLAN 2.115): these keys and no others, so one written as CSS writes one (`spread`) is an error at the key, where it is written.

x.description: How far right of the node it falls; left where it is negative. None by default.

y.description: How far below the node it falls; above where it is negative. None by default.

blur.description: How soft its edge is: the blur's radius, twice the deviation of the Gaussian it is drawn with. None by default.

color.description: A theme color: black by default.

opacity.description: How dark it is, from 0 to 1: 1 by default.

Clip.description: Clip to the node's box, or to SVG path data.

Placement.description: Where a node goes. One placement wins: `rect`, else `in`, else `col`/`row` (SPEC §3.4). Grid cells and slots are theme-managed; `rect` is an explicit override (lint W301 in template-managed states). In a container (`parent`), `col`/`row` and `area` are its grid's, `rect` is relative to a frame's padding, and a stack places its children itself, as a shape places its words.

in.description: Named slot in the state's layout template, or `canvas` or `grid`.

parent.description: The container this node is in: a `stack`, `grid`, `frame`, or `group` (ADR-0008). A text's may be a shape, other than a line or an arrow: the text is the shape's words, which it places in the room inside it, with no other key of `at` (PLAN 2.108).

index.description: Order among the container's children, as CSS `order`: ascending, default 0, ties in `nodes` order.

area.description: A named area of the grid container this node is in.

Range2.description: A grid index or an inclusive [start, end] range (1-based).

Rect.description: [x, y, w, h] in canvas units.

Align.description: Alignment within a slot or cell. Vertical anchors include typographic ones (SPEC §3.4).

NodeTransition.description: How this node moves between two states that both show it (SPEC §3.9).

PresetRef.description: A theme motion preset by name, or a preset with parameters.

Duration.description: Milliseconds, or a named theme duration ("fast", "standard", "slow").

Easing.description: Named theme easing or a cubic Bézier [x1, y1, x2, y2].

Spring.description: Named theme spring or explicit parameters.

SplitUnit.description: What a choreographed entrance splits its target into. A text's `paragraphs` are the stretches its hard line breaks end, a list's items (deck format 0.27, theme format 0.17).

LookParams.description: Numbers a look sets on what its unit draws.

progress.description: How much of each outline a shape strokes is drawn, from where the outline starts.

AnimTracks.description: Per-property keyframe tracks within a state, each property a look's (SPEC §3.9): `opacity`, `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`, and `progress`. They never track to the next state.

t.description: Milliseconds from the start of the track.

v.description: Value; its type must match the property.

FormatLayout.description: A node's layout in one of the deck's formats (SPEC §3.4, ADR-0020): where it goes, how big, how it is turned, a container's tracks and spacing, and a text's lines. Each property takes the place of the node's own of the same name in that format; a property its type does not have is E106, as anywhere on the node.

Padding.description: One length for every side, or 2–4 lengths CSS-style.

Tracks.description: A count of equal tracks, or each track's size.

TextStyle.description: What a text node, or a run, changes about its role's look (SPEC §3.6): the role's own properties, by name; each replaces the role's. `family` names a theme family and `color` a theme color token or role. A literal color, and any `size`, is a pixel value: theme-legal only in `overrides` (lint W300 elsewhere).

italic.description: Set in the family's italic face (SPEC §3.5), or, `false`, upright. None is synthesized: a family without one sets the text upright (lint W231).

leading.description: Line height as a multiple of size.

style.description: What this run changes about its role's look, after the node's `style` when the run is set in the node's role (SPEC §3.6).

features.description: OpenType features for this run, after the node's (SPEC §3.3, PLAN 1.38): `kern: false` sets a pair loose, `ss01: true` a word in a stylistic set. A change of them shapes the run apart from its neighbors, as a change of font does.

axes.description: Variable-font axis values for this run, after the node's (PLAN 1.38).

link.description: Where the run goes when it is followed (SPEC §3.5, PLAN 2.70): a web address, or a state of the deck. It is drawn underlined.

quote.description: The value of a data source the run's text is (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0019, PLAN 2.72): its text is the figure as last set, which every write sets again from the data.

Link.description: Where a link goes (PLAN 2.70): a web address (`https:`, `http:`, or `mailto:`), which the player opens in a new window, or a state of the deck, which it shows.

Quote.description: A value of a data source that a run quotes (ADR-0019): a cell of the source, read as a chart reads it, through its `dataTransform`, written by `format`.

data.description: The source, as a chart names it: `@` and its id.

dataTransform.description: Steps the source is read through, as a chart's (SPEC §3.10).

row.description: The row: the one whose columns hold these values, or an index from 0, negative from the end (`-1`, the last). Without one, the table has one row.

column.description: The column whose cell it is.

format.description: How the cell is written: a number format for a number, a date format for a date (SPEC §3.7). Without one, as a chart writes a category.

anyOf.description: The one row whose columns hold these values.

QuoteKey.description: A value a quote's row is found by.

TextFit.description: What a text node does when its text does not fit (SPEC §3.4).

Wrap.description: How a text's lines break where its words run past its width (SPEC §3.5).

TextSplit.description: What a text node's own `split` divides it into for motion.

ListItem.description: A paragraph of a text as an item of a list (SPEC §3.5, ADR-0018): bulleted or numbered, at a level, 0 the outermost. Its marker and indent are the theme's (`type.lists`).

Code.description: What makes a text code (PLAN 2.131, ADR-0029): the language its words are written in.

language.description: The language its words are written in, a lowercase name: one Scaena knows, by its name or an alias (`rust`, `rs`, `c++`), `plain` for none, or any other, which the generic scanner colors (`scaena_core::code`).

Connect.description: What a connector joins (PLAN 2.109): the node it runs from, the node it runs to, and how.

route.description: `straight`, the default, runs between the two boxes along the line from middle to middle; `elbow` leaves one box by the side that faces the other and turns at right angles; `curved` leaves and meets the boxes as an elbow does, a cubic curve through the elbow's corners (PLAN 2.128, deck format 0.27).

Route.description: How a connector runs between what it joins (PLAN 2.109, 2.128).

LineEnds.description: A line's or an arrow's two ends (PLAN 2.128), as a presentation app's line endpoints.

LineEnd.description: What one end of a line is drawn with, sized from its stroke: nothing, a filled `arrow`head, an `open` one of two strokes, or a filled `circle`, `square`, or `diamond` on the end.

ImageFit.description: How an image meets its box.

oneOf.description: Fills the box, cutting what overflows (the default).
Fits inside the box, whole.
Stretched to the box.

ImageMask.description: The shape an image shows inside (PLAN 2.113): an oval, or a polygon of the shape library (`scaena_core::inserts::polygons`), by its name.

ImageAdjust.description: How an image's light and color are adjusted (PLAN 2.117): each from -1 to 1, where 0, or none, leaves the picture as it is.

exposure.description: Brighter or darker, as a camera's exposure: 1 is two stops brighter, -1 two darker.

contrast.description: The lights lighter and the darks darker, or both nearer the middle: -1 is a flat gray.

saturation.description: More color, or less: -1 is black and white, 1 twice the color.

warmth.description: Warmer, toward orange, or cooler, toward blue, as a camera's white balance.

Pin.description: A pin the engine draws on an image (ADR-0030, decision 13): any image may take one.

at.description: Where its tip stands, [x, y] in fractions of the picture, as `crop` is.

label.description: Its label, set in the theme's `label` role beside it; none, or `""`, gives none.

color.description: A theme color: the accent by default.

CreditPlace.description: Where an image's credit is drawn (ADR-0030, decision 14).

oneOf.description: On a card in the picture's bottom-left corner (the default).
As a line under the picture, inside the node's box.

ChartKind.description: v1 chart kinds (SPEC §3.7); waffle and heatmap are deferred. A `slope` compares two states, a line a series from the first to the second, both ends labeled and the change said; a `range` spans the value axis at each category, a dumbbell between its series or each value with its `interval` (PLAN 1.30); a `weather` chart draws a forecast, a column for each period, its sky's icon and its figures (ADR-0030).

ChartOrient.description: Which way a chart's bars run (SPEC §3.7, PLAN 1.29).

oneOf.description: Up from the baseline, the categories along the foot.
Across from the baseline, the categories down the side.

Encoding.description: One chart channel bound to a data field.

scale.description: Theme data palette name for color encodings (categorical | sequential | diverging).

Sort.description: A sort direction, or a field to sort by.

Interval.description: The fields that hold each value's interval on a `range` (SPEC §3.7, PLAN 1.30).

low.description: The field of its low end.

high.description: The field of its high end.

Facet.description: How a chart splits into small multiples (SPEC §3.7, PLAN 1.31).

field.description: The field whose values split the data, a panel each, in the order they first appear.

columns.description: How many panels stand in a row; unset, the count that makes each panel nearest 3:2.

Projected.description: Which of a line's or an area's rows are projected: a forecast, or an estimate (SPEC §3.7). The rows whose `field` holds `value`, or a true one when no value is given. The line runs dashed from the last actual point through them, the area under them is lighter, and their value labels say they are estimates.

value.description: What `field` holds in a projected row; `true` when unset.

note.description: What a projected value's label says after the value; the theme's `charts.projected.note` when unset.

collide.description: How labels that collide resolve (lint W310 otherwise).

LabelShow.description: Which values a chart prints. `auto` (the theme's `charts.label.show`, else by kind) puts the data on the marks: every bar, dot, and slice; a line's or an area's first and last; a scatter's none.

Legend.description: Where a chart's legend stands, alone or with a title (SPEC §3.7).

LegendPlace.description: Where a legend stands. `auto` is the theme's `charts.legend.place`, else `direct`. `direct` names each series at its end, beside the plot, where a chart has ends: a line, an area, or a stacked bar; any other chart places it `top`.

place.description: `top` when unset: a titled legend is a legend, not labels at the series' ends.

title.description: Printed before the entries, in the legend's role.

Annotation.description: A chart annotation (SPEC §3.7): a rule, a band, a callout, or a highlight, in the theme's `charts.annotation` style.

at.description: Where it stands, by kind: a rule at `x` or `y`, a band from one to another of either, a callout at `x` (and `y`, or a `series`), a highlight on categories `x` and series, or, naming neither, on every mark.

text.description: What it says; a highlight says nothing.

AnnotationAt.description: An annotation's place: a category or an x value (a number, or a date as ISO 8601), a value on the value axis, and a series, each one or several by kind.

Place3.description: One value, or several: a band's two ends, or what a highlight picks out.

Scalar.description: A number, or text: a category, a series, or a date.

Weather.description: What a `weather` chart draws (SPEC §3.7, ADR-0030 decision 19): a column for each period of a forecast, across the box, or a row down a box taller than wide, each its name, its sky's icon, and its figures.

fields.description: The columns each part reads, where they are not the forecast's own.

units.description: The units it shows its figures in: the source's by default. They convert at layout.

show.description: The parts each period shows, in this order; `period`, `sky`, `high`, `low`, and `chance` when unset.

every.description: Hours between columns of a forecast by the hour; unset, 1, 2, 3, or 6, the least that fits.

band.description: The theme color a highlighted period stands on: `surface-2` when unset.

WeatherFields.description: The columns a `weather` chart reads its parts from (ADR-0030, decision 18).

sky.description: The WMO code of each period's sky: `sky`.

high.description: The high: `high` by the day, `temperature` by the hour.

chance.description: The chance of rain, in percent: `rain`.

day.description: Whether an hour is in daylight: `day`.

WeatherPart.description: A part of a `weather` chart's period.

oneOf.description: Its name: the weekday, or the hour.
The sky's icon.
The sky in words.
The chance of rain, with a drop where it is 10% or more.

title.description: The header's text; the field's name when unset.

format.description: How its numbers or dates print (docs/spec/format.md).

align.description: Where its text sits across the column; `end` for numbers, else `start`, when unset.

ColumnAlign.description: Where a column's text sits across it.

ShaderParam.description: A shader parameter: a number, or a name its kind lists (a gradient's `shape`).

slide.description: The slide this state builds on: its first state's id. A state without one starts a slide named by its own id.

from.description: Track from this state instead of the previous one (branch).

layout.description: Layout template name from the theme.

furniture.description: Whether the slide shows the deck's furniture, its number and footer (deck format 0.19, ADR-0028): `false` hides them, `true` shows them on a layout the theme leaves them off. A slide's first state says it for the whole slide.

props.description: Per-node property deltas for this state. Keys are node ids.

remove.description: Nodes that exit in this state.

hold.description: Auto-advance dwell in ms (video and kiosk). It wins over its beat's `duration`.

notes.description: Speaker notes, which a presenter reads over its beat's (SPEC §2.6).

StateMode.description: How a state relates to the one before it (SPEC §2.2).

oneOf.description: Declare changes only; unchanged properties track forward.
Everything explicit; nothing tracks.

Transition.description: The transition into a state: a bare duration, or the object form (SPEC §3.9). A state without one cuts.

style.description: How the slide changes, as a presentation app's slide transitions do (PLAN 2.111): the slide left and the slide entered each drawn whole, one moving, uncovered, or faded over the other, nothing morphing between them. Without one, what both states show morphs.

direction.description: Which way a `push`, a `cover`, a `reveal`, a `wipe`, a `circleWave`, or a `diamondWave` moves: `left`, the default, which brings the slide entered in from the right, `right`, `up`, or `down`. A `radial`'s hand starts so the slide entered shows first on that side: straight up for `left`, at three o'clock for `up`, six for `right`, and nine for `down`.

oneOf.description: The slide entered fades in over the slide left.
The slide entered pushes the slide left off the canvas.
The slide entered slides in over the slide left.
The slide left slides away, uncovering the slide entered.
An edge sweeps across, the slide entered behind it.
Circles grow across the slide, the slide entered inside them (PLAN 2.149).
Circles grow in a wave across the slide, the way `direction` goes.
Diamonds grow across the slide together.
Diamonds grow in a wave across the slide, the way `direction` goes.
A clock's hand sweeps round the slide's middle, the slide entered in its wake.

TransitionDirection.description: Which way a slide transition moves (PLAN 2.111).

StateDelta.description: The delta a state applies to one node: any node type's property, or null to delete it. An object value merges one level into the tracked one (the …Delta forms), so its keys are optional and null deletes one. An empty delta shows the node with its defaults (SPEC §2.2). Whether a property belongs to the node's type is checked on the resolved state (PLAN 1.2).

TransformDelta.description: `Transform` in a state's delta: it merges one level into the tracked value, so every key is optional and null deletes one (SPEC §2.2).
